title: Every vector subspace has a complement
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $V$ a $k$-vector space, and $P\subseteq V$ a vector subspace (a subset containing $0$ and closed under addition and scalar multiplication). There exists a vector subspace $Q\subseteq V$ such that every $v\in V$ has a unique expression $v=p+q$ with $p\in P$ and $q\in Q$; equivalently $V=P\oplus Q$. No finite-dimensionality assumption is imposed.
